classifications.runtime_defect: A demonstrated runtime mechanism, repaired, with controls.
classifications.bound_exhausted_cause_unknown: The retained receipts show a bound that ran out. The runtime or fixture failed closed. No control reproduces the historical stall or identifies its cause. Later passing samples do not explain the failure.
classifications.defect_demonstrated_attribution_unresolv: A real defect is demonstrated, but the historical receipts contradict the condition that the control reproduces.
classifications.did_not_recur: The bound was exhausted historically and the cause is unknown. The instrumented soak exercised the same shape and it did not recur. This is not an explanation.
classifications.fixture_defect_open: A demonstrated fixture mechanism without a repair yet. A named leaf owns the repair.
classifications.input_runtime_explained: Retained timestamps show that the input runtime, not a stall, exhausted the bound. No repair is owed.

caller-cleanup-k145/candidate-v2-full: assert -9 == 0, PID TERM then PID KILL
cases.mechanism: The k145 peer ignored TERM until its child declared readiness. With no declaration, the k151 control reproduces return code -9 with PID KILL, but the peer then prints no child PID. Both historical runs printed the child PID: 34536 in k145 run 179b4702 and 16638 in k132 run fc704d02. The peer prints that PID only after it leaves its readiness loop. So readiness was reached before KILL, and the never-ready condition is not the historical cause. Late readiness followed by slow exit is possible but unproven.
cases.repair: Commit d5251d7 (k143) honours TERM before child readiness. That repairs the demonstrated defect, not an identified historical cause.

observations: same run: test_review_worker_rejects_fork_before_creation, owner 4100 left in worker_capture._owners
cases.mechanism: The parent made 40 WNOHANG polls about 6 ms apart, the last 64 ms before the 0.3 s deadline. It made no further syscall until after the deadline, and the receipt finished 140 ms after it. The soak load sampler, another process, woke 161 ms late over the same window. Its next-largest delay in 808 samples was 12 ms. So a host-wide stall of about 160 ms crossed the deadline. The runtime then correctly sent no signal. The fixture child waits on signal.pause() and the fixture has no cleanup for a child the runtime did not signal. The child stayed alive as PID 4100, and its owner record failed the next test.
